I'm in a bit of a pickle.

I'm nearly 34 years old. I'm white. I'm responsible. I'm healthy. I love my husband more than I could accurately convey. But we've got a problem.

My husband is a good man; perhaps a bit too blindly trusting and hopelessly devoted to a fault. He treats me well. For the most part, I feel valued and respected for my contributions in the home. Having both come from turbulent upbringings, we have a propensity to avoid unnecessary escalations. This is both a blessing and a curse. We'll call my husband "Peter".

I was 25 when we met. Peter is a couple years younger but wise beyond his years. We were very honest with one another about our goals. I made it unmistakeably clear that I wanted to start a family before the age of 30. He agreed but we weren't about to rush into anything. Eventually, I made a huge sacrifice and moved in with him. ( I'll avoid details of said sacrifice as I would like to retain some anonymity. Just know that my sacrifice involved up and leaving an established life in another city. ) Once living together, we grew even closer with each day. We both toiled away at our respective careers for some time. I made it clear that my career came secondary to our plans. His career advanced marvellously! ( I am so incredibly proud of all of his accomplishments as I know that they did not come without much anguish. I supported his growth and continue to do so. )

While my heart was fully committed, it wasn't put onto paper until I turned 31. He insisted that we delay having children until it was on paper, yet it took him years to propose despite knowing my still unfulfilled goals. Only after I strongly reminded him of my goals did he eventually propose.

A few months after our marriage became official, we inherited a problem.

The problem truly began much sooner but it was not yet our problem. Peter's only brother is a heroin addict, a violent sociopath, and the emotional equivalent of a fourteen year old. We'll call him "Sam". Sam is younger than Peter.

Sam has been in and out of jail for drug and alcohol related offences. He had been living with his mother; a frail disabled single woman. He had been staying in her large house. Her being disabled, she could not navigate certain areas of the house. Sam took full advantage of this. His upstairs room, a foul smelling sty, was beyond her reach. It became his drug den.

Sam just turned 25 when he moved in with us. Peter begged for me to accept his brother into our happy home. I reluctantly yet gracefully agreed after making my concerns known. Peter gave an estimated time-line of six months. The goal was to get Sam out of his tiny heroin infested town and onto better opportunities. An agreement was signed by all parties. Sam is turning 27 in a few days. Not one condition of that signed agreement has been met.

Sam is not clean. Sam uses in our home. Sam looks and smells like shit. He has a job but barely. He is months behind on rent and eats all of our food. If he isn't eating our food, he is buying himself copious amounts of sugary crap in true junkie style. He requires rides EVERYWHERE; to and from work, especially. ( I've been toting him around for two years. ) He has a non working car parked in our driveway, though. His enabling mother bought him yet another car. He drunkenly wrecked the other three. But he won't take the driving test to regain his license- even after his mother paid off his thousands of dollars in court and dmv fees. She isn't rich by any means. She is allowing herself to be driven into the poorhouse. She will enable him before she pays her bills or loans (including loans made by us). He will be sitting happy while her heat is turned off. He will easily put on the concerned son mask in a sickly sweet display when he feels it might offer a social boost. A grown man talking baby talk to his "mommy" makes me uncomfortable.

Peter keeps having these "talks" with Sam that I am not allowed to be a part of. I am excluded solely because Sam insists that I am too intense. Sam insists this because I once (about two years ago) responded to a verbal attack with equal measure. This is when my faith in my husband began eroding. Sam was screaming at Peter. Peter had dared bring up Sam's odd junkie behavior and a verbal argument ensued. I run my own home based business. I see Sam a whole lot more than Peter does. I added an observation to the mix in a calm and collected manner. Sam screeched at me "YOU DO NOT FUCKING MATTER!!! SHUT THE FUCK UP!". My husband fell completely silent. Somewhat in shock that Peter would allow this, I responded with a shaky "Who the fuck do you think you are?! You're SHIT! You're a childish little shit!" before leaving for a very much needed long solo drive in the country.

About once a month, the brothers meet in private to discuss Sam and his recovery. Nothing is ever accomplished. There were talks about him seeking a sober living home but that quickly devolved into "searching for a room mate". Peter relays some details. It is difficult to know what is and isn't truthful when it comes from an addict, let alone a sociopath.

Since we legally married, Peter and I have been trying for a child. I'll admit that there has been far less trying as of late. I just don't feel connected to him as I once did. I do not feel that he has my back on any of this and I am so completely turned off. I had an early miscarriage in April. That was rough. We had just found out we were pregnant before our first solo vacation ever... and I began miscarrying on the plane. I bled the entire time. We came home to a junkie melting on the sofa. I'm not trying to break apart his family. I've done more than my part to help his entire family. Most of my every day involves serving his family in some way.
